correctness.rationale: In a state returning after three synchronous updates, any site that is ever excited must cycle 1,2,0, and a site that is never excited must stay at 0. An edge between the two classes would excite the latter; connectedness therefore makes all sites cycle unless all are zero. The excitation at each site's resting time is exactly the presence of its initial cyclic successor in its open neighborhood. With exact row palettes specified, this is a per-column test; inclusion–exclusion forces every color of each specified palette to occur. The finite integer computation is independent of n: a separate nine-bit subset-zeta aggregation reproduced every coefficient, and literal updates on all states at widths 1–3 gave 6, 72, 2562. The formula gives 119880 and 5109306 at widths 4 and 5. Every nonfixed returning phase has orbit size three. After normalizing by 27^n the two largest surviving corrections have bases 18/27 and 14/27, proving the stated leading term and remainder.
residual_risks: The result is for labelled time-zero states with synchronous threshold-one updates, not transient basins or spatial symmetry orbits. The all-positive-width result does not address n=0.
